html:
Who He Is

Moran Steppe Fire is a Shavan from Reis County, a blue-eyed, gusty and restless warrior who spent twenty years in the saddle before the events of the cycle began. Sir Gage, a knight of the Litlands, explained the nickname as follows: Moran's burrows are like a fire in the steppe - they will flare up and will not stop until everything burns out. Moran did not have a noble family, but by will and courage, according to the same Gage, only “by the hair” was inferior to Count Damir Reis and was unconditionally loyal to him while he was alive. In Rebecca's story, he is called the Count's right hand, and Gage describes Reis as a county ruled by two "iron hands": the right hand is the Earl of Damir, the left hand is the Shavan Moran.

Neymir the Werewolf, who for the first time found himself in the leader's tent, saw in him a man who could not stand still for a minute: Moran measured the tent with his feet, crossed his belt with his fingers, and when he froze, he still felt a bubbling force in him, "like boiling water under the lid." (Neimir) Naimir's experience was that such hot warriors die first, but Moran broke this rule: twenty years of fighting, and is still alive.

The “Soul of the West”

In August 1774, Moran arrived with Count Damir Reis to negotiate with the Litlands at their Lacy estate near Faunterra. He immediately drew attention to Rebecca Litland. At dawn, he called her racing to the apple orchard; then he put an apple on his top, Rebecca fired, and he caught her arrow on the fly. Moran said she has "the soul of a Westerner is free." Later, Rebecca admitted to herself that she was offended at first, and then realized that he was right. Later he found her in a meadow behind a grove and kissed her; Rebecca felt "only fire and sweetness". The two of them left for the fields, and she only returned home at dawn. When Rebecca said no, Moran backed down.

The negotiations turned out to be a trap (an ambush in Lacey): the Litlandes, having received a letter from which it followed that the North had "bought" the Duke of Litland, decided to kill the ambassadors. (Ambush at Lacey; House Litland) At the last dinner, Moran, having heard something wrong, shouted to Rebecca: "What was in the letter?!" - and she, realizing everything, shouted "Run!". Lord Coss fired a crossbow attached to the table and mortally wounded Count Damir (who died two days later). In the fight, Moran was rumored to have killed five Lithuanians, including Gage's sire, and threw himself out the window. When Coss pointed the crossbow at Moran running towards the stable, Rebecca hit the bottom of the bed, and the bolt went into the sky. The chase lasted for several days, but Moran left. So Rebecca saved his life twice: with her cry and with this blow. From the ambush, he returned alone, so that the whole horde knew this story from his words; Moran himself confirmed it: "In the jackals-Lithuanian daughter turned out to be a man."

In "Only One Star"

In the autumn of 1774, two ambassadors of Reiss appeared to Emperor Adrian and announced that Count Damir was "sinisterly killed by the Litlands at the emperor's acquiescence", and Moran the Steppe Fire, the new ruler of Reiss, spoke through their mouths. One of the ambassadors there, in the throne room, stabbed Count Rantigar of the Sunset Coast, loyal to Adrian. Soon Moran crossed Holliwell and invaded Litland; according to reports, about thirty thousand horsemen followed him, Holliwell's warriors, Mills and, according to rumors, the Sunset Coast joined the horde. (Hollywell) Adrian marched into Litland with spark regiments and, together with Prince Hector of Shimmery on 2 December 1774, inflicted a heavy defeat on the horde near Melorange: the Shavans flew into a trap from the wagon with spark infantry. According to Neymir, a quarter of the horde died and another quarter was wounded; the horde lost its camp, supplies, and prey.

"A Doll on the Throne"

A leader who does not retreat

In one autumn, the horde ravaged half of Litland: seven cities were plundered, three field battles were won. Moran took the crossings over the sacred Halliwell and led the riders so fast that the Dukes of Little Earth did not have time to assemble a large army. He taught the Shavans to fight not only for the sake of booty, but "for freedom itself", infected them with hatred for the "lord tyrant" and the Lithuanian "shakals", and then the riders, according to Naymir, loved him as a native father.

After the defeat at Melorange, the starving Shavans waited for orders to retreat. Moran gathered them and announced that the war was on: the enemy must be lured out of the walls and trampled, and only then can you return home. When the Gants Jantey (three hundred horsemen) and Barok (four hundred) declared that they were leaving, Moran threw a knife at Barok's throat, stabbed Jantey in three strokes, cut off both heads and vowed to lead the horde to victory: whoever does not go alone will have to bear it. That same night, a hundred of Barok's Shavans attacked his tent and were killed, and a hundred of Jantaeus' fugitives were overtaken in the field by Moran's horsemen and shot. Surviving rebels and deserters were hung from trees around the camp, breaking the bones of their hands and feet; later, when there were not enough trees, new deserters were pinned with nails to the dug-in pillars.

Many in the horde hated Moran. Ganta Cort believed that the chief out of a thirst for revenge would lead the horde into the jungle for destruction, and said that the whole war was being waged "because of the woman" - because of the Litland girl, which the chief was unable to take along with Melorange. (Ganta Kort)

Satellites

Moran ordered each major gang to send him a pair of the best warriors for reconnaissance, and the Ghante Grose ordered to surround the camp with a ring of dozers, overfish all enemy scouts and "find him a birdhouse", that is, a dove. (Ganta Thunderstorm) Ganta Cort sent Neymir and Chara, the Satellites, with a secret order to kill the leader. (Ganta Kort; Neimir) Moran knew their past: that Neymir was formerly called a Werewolf and could pass for a resident of any land except the north, and Chara was nicknamed Without Fear. When he heard that the pair was worth seven warriors, he decided, “Seven is my favorite number,” and sent seven scouts, one of whom was Sputnik.

When Neymir demanded to explain why intelligence was needed, and threatened to refuse otherwise, Moran, to his surprise, laughed, said that they were the “soul of the West”, and revealed to them the plan: to find out in which port the Shimmer fleet was standing, burn it, lock up the southerners in Melorange and hit the defenseless and rich Shimmery. He showed them a map with three harbors (Maple, Colmin, Rain Forest), gave them a purse of money and told Neymir to give Char for his althessa. Asked about Rebecca, he replied:

“Sooner or later I’ll take mine. The West has a long memory.”

The satellites were captured by Hector, who had a letter of “one gang”, warning about the scouts. Under threat of torture, Neymir issued a plan. Meanwhile, the horde secretly went into the jungle, moved without bonfires and buried the killed Litland scouts so that the vultures would not betray her. Hector, believing in the plan, went out of Melorange to the Rain Forest - and the horde struck him in the flank and in the back, turned the southerners into a fugitive and captured the entire train. The Lithuanians came out of the walls to the rescue of the Allies, and the Shavans had to turn around, which saved the Shimmerians from complete extermination.

After the victory, Moran was already preparing a siege: he was going to build stonemasons, set fire to something in the city with fire arrows every night, and let the prisoners (more than three hundred) go to Melorange with the news that any citizen could leave by paying twenty pounds of provisions. Upon learning of the Savior of the Companions, the Sorcerer, who baked people with a touch, Moran spat ("Keep me steppe from such friends"), but admitted that sorcerers can be useful against the "pigalica from the North" and the Origin wolves. (Mik)

Injuries

Neymir compared the facts: the horde left the camp the day before Sputnik was captured, and Moran needed the pigeon before the reconnaissance. So the chief wrote the letter to Hector, and the Sputniks were bait. Neymir caught up with Moran and threw the charge in his face; Moran grabbed the sword, but Neymir outstripped him and cut his thigh to the bone. Chara pointed the horse at the fallen chief, and the hoof shattered his knee. While the Thunderstorm with a dozen riders rushed in pursuit, Chara tried to finish off Moran with arrows, but he crawled away behind the horse's corpse. Satellites failed to kill him.

The Siege of Melorange and the Meeting with Minerva

The crippled Moran laid siege to Melorange. They did not attempt to storm the city of Shavan, but a dozen stones struck it day and night with stones and burning resin. The townspeople who carried twenty pounds of food, Moran released alive, until the Litlands blocked this flow. Thousands of horsemen rode along the walls with dead heads on spears, inciting fear. In March 1775, he offered the Litlands peace: one hundred ephes for each rider, and for himself - the bride, Rebecca. Rebecca's father was ready to agree, and she took refuge in the quarter of the spark regiment of General William Davey. (William Davy) By the spring, under the leadership of Moran, there were already about forty thousand riders: after the news of the death of Adrian and new victories, new Shavans reached the horde. The lame chief could hardly hold his saddle and could not fight, but the Shavans forgave him for his successes.

In the spring, the Empress Minerva personally came to him by train to negotiate with Captain Shatterhand, Kair Jemis Lilliday and six Guards. Moran brought out four hundred horsemen; they circled around the ambassadors, clicking whips, and poured around them a shaft of the bones of the legs of the killed enemies: "so that on the Star they crawled like worms." The chief drew a spear on the land of Halliwell and demanded that the whole steppe part of Litland be written down behind Steppe to Melorange. Minerva responded by offering him a bouquet of lilies and a vassal oath. She recalled that in the spring, Holliwell spills and there are only two crossings - the Cool Threshold and the Julian Bridge, where you can move troops on the rails in three days. She showed pigeons with orders to General Alexis not to occupy the Cool Threshold and to Duke Origin not to send troops to the West: the birds would not fly away if the ambassadors were killed. The regiment at Julian's bridge really stood ready, and the threat of Origin was a bluff. Moran demanded Melorange, trophies and Lithuanian gold; Minerva promised only that the Litlands would no longer encroach on Shepherd's Meadow. He finally said about Rebecca, "I love her." Minerva said that it will be up to Rebecca to decide, and she will bless the marriage if she agrees. Moran hit the lance of the satellite, who wanted to object, picked up the abandoned bouquet, served it to Minerva and said: "Your Majesty." He lifted the siege, released the prisoners, and took the horde for Holliwell.

In "Yanmei Hunt" and "Humans and Gods"

Ray - Roy

Count Vittor Shayland discussed with his wife whether to help Moran with gold: the chavans murmured that they did not take Melorange, and the money would make the chief a debtor to Shayland. Iona talked him out of it. Ganta Birai, who had defected to Adrian's side, told the lord that Moran would rather bite off his hand than fight for it, and promised to persuade the king's side: "Moran is now lame and weak - a great time to change the leader!"

After taking the horde away, Moran settled in Rei-Roy, the capital of Reis, where he ruled with the young Count Johan Reis. His representative in the House and at court was Ganta Thunderstorm, who called himself "the whip of Moran." Erwin Origin told Grose that the crippled chief "smells with weakness", that Minerva had driven him "with words and a single regiment" and that the Gaunt Dung was already breathing into Morana's back; The storm flared up, but eventually agreed that leaving Melorange was reasonable.

According to rumors, Sputnik broke the will of the leader along with his legs, and the refusal of the “girl Litland” deprived him of male power. Ganta Court had beaten him a month earlier to a raid on Shimmery, weakened by the Labelins, but Moran replied, "We will fight when I say, and with whomever I choose." (Ganta Kort) At the council in his tent, he demanded that Juhan directly recount the rumors, praised him for his honesty, and Cort, who had again started talking about bad times, threw wine in his face: "Next time it will be a knife." He explained his strategy as follows: in the world now five forces — the Crown, the North, the Center, the Steppe and the Puppeteer with the Rings — and all except the Steppe, are at war with each other; when the enemies cut each other, the main force will remain Shavans.

While seeing Groz in the spring of 1775 in the capital, Moran admonished him: the central lands hold the Shavans as savages and speak to them only when there is no better interlocutor, "but you must teach them to reckon with us." Groza boasted that he had done it in a month. On May 29, 1775, when the House, after the deposition of Adrian, chose the contenders for the throne, among the shouts from the hall was “Moran is the leader of the whole Steppe, he must rule!”. In June, Adrian, who sought the support of the Shavans, rejected the idea of moving the capital to Rei-Roy, "the lair of the rebel and rebel", who led the horde against him. Around June 1, Groza made a deal with Erwin: if Origin conquers Almera, the gauntlet will bring the Steppe Fire to his side, and on June 20–21, although Almera was not taken, confirmed the alliance in exchange for all the gold of the Shayland banks.

Erwin Origin compared Moran to Gett from the steppe legend - a leader who, with the help of magical power, became a monster and flooded the world with blood. (The Legend of Gett) Erwin feared that Paul, the messenger of the Puppeteer, would arm the horde with the Wilhelm's Fingers. He asked Rebecca to marry Moran; she refused and showed a capsule of poison. Later, she did go to Rei-Roy to get ahead of the heretics, but arrived after the massacre of the leader: Paul, according to Alanis, took advantage of her arrival to repeat the "presentation" with Eternity for that part of the horde that did not see the death of Moran.

Death

Paul got to Rei-Roy first. His unit - Paul, Knuth, Fly, Chara and Alanis Almera - Johan's men were detained near the city; Paul called himself the giver, who brought the leader of the two slaves. Hearing the name of the commander, Moran understood who he was dealing with, ordered to disarm the aliens (they found bags of Objects), surrounded the area with two selected hundreds of archers and, relying on the hand of Johan, went out to meet him. Paul called him “the chief cripple” and declared himself a god from the underworld; Moran laughed, "You're not a god. You're a creep. I was told about you,” and called him only a sorcerer of the Puppeteer, whose teeth were torn out.

Moran ordered the first hundred to fire, but the arrows froze in a cloud of black flies surrounding Paul. Then the leader with an unexpected speed for the cripple cut Paul around the neck. The blade, followed by Moran’s hand and body, darkened and frozen in the cloud: an object called Eternity threw him out of the flow of time. The horror was forever imprinted on his face. Paul declared the leader deposed, pushed him into the chest, and Moran began to fall backwards "slower than the sun moves through the sky." Paul distributed the Shavans of the Persians and led the horde under the name of the Ganta Pnoi. Later, standing at the "black, fallen out of time corpse of Moran", Paul arranged the second distribution of the Rings; and arrived in Rei-Roy Rebecca, he turned into the same frozen figure with the words that he would fulfill her desire to connect with her beloved.

Moran himself, contrary to Erwin's guess, never led the horde to the North: the captive old men told him that he remained in Rei-Roy "as an invincible guard", and with him - "a strange maiden". At the end of June 1775, Erwin found their frozen bodies at the gates of Rei-Roy: Rebecca froze in a jump over the saddle, and Moran - a foot from the ground, falling on her back. Erwin was ambushed by the persunos near them.

The Shadow of the Great Tree

The news that Paul "killed" Moran and led the horde reached Minerva. Alanis, who was at Paul, believed that the souls of Moran and Becky did not fall on the Star and remain locked in bodies, “for years ... for centuries.” At the council of the Horde, Johan Reis and Ganta Court boasted that they would be able to do what Moran could not: defeat the Yankees. Adrian, who sympathized with the Steppes, considered Moran and Paul "rebel leaders" who stirred up the Steppe, and hoped after Paul's death to return the horde to the bosom of the empire with the help of the Birai gant.

In "Fantasies"

In the stories “Fantasies”, which the author calls the possible fates of the heroes, Moran is mentioned in the “Device” (Spring 1776). After the death of the Ganta, the largest pack of Shavans joined the Ganta of Cort. (Ganta Kort) He declared himself a warrior of the Pramatery of Helena and claimed that all the great shavannas - Paul, Moran and Court himself - came from her.

Personality

Moran is a brave, cunning and cruel leader who is able to sacrifice his best people for victory and mercilessly deal with the rebels. They burn their dead, not bury them. He is quick-tempered, but knows how to wait; despises wagging and appreciates when they speak directly. At the same time, he is proud and not deprived of a kind of nobility: he retreated from Rebecca when she refused, and promised life to the besieged townspeople if they themselves open the gates. His hatred of the Litlands and his feelings for Rebecca were equally driving his war: “The West has a long memory,” he said.

Trivia

  • Moran's favorite number is seven; therefore, he sent exactly seven scouts to Melorange: one three, two singles, and one pair.
  • According to the "Guide to the Lands of Polari", in Reis to break a man's legs is considered almost as grave a sin as murder, and to make the moving motionless without need is a great evil. Moran was injured twice: Satellites crippled his legs, and Paul deprived him of movement forever.
  • At a meeting of the Supreme Court, when Lady-in-the-Dark called a candidate for the lords of Erwin Origin, someone from the hall shouted: “Moran is the leader of the whole Steppe, he must rule!”
  • Killed Litland scouts hordes during a secret march through the jungle buried, although usually shavana throw the corpses of enemies jackals: vultures over the bodies would give away where the army goes.

Appearances

  • "The Soul of the West" - the first appearance (an ambush in Lacey).
  • "Only one Star" - mentioned: Ambassadors Moran, the invasion of Litland, the defeat at Melorange.
  • "A Doll on the Throne" - acts in the chapters "Satellite" (the point of view of Neymir and Chara) and in the chapter on negotiations with Minerva.
  • "Janmei Hunt" and "Humans and Gods" - Rei-Roy, Gantt Council, meeting with Paul.
  • "The Shadow of the Great Tree" is mentioned; his frozen body stands in Rei-Roy.
  • "Fantasies" is mentioned in the "Device".
